blocks.instructionalPurpose: Define a problem, test a design against criteria and constraints, and improve it across iterations; optionally record each design's results in a named measurement table. Learner action: Complete both available observation records, source labels and the hand-drawn graph before leaving this activity.

accessibility.textAlternative: Build and compare two low-voltage flashlight-switch designs. Use repeated tests to choose or improve a design. Light when closed: Closed-switch light successes, at least 4 trials. Dark when open: Open-switch dark successes, at least 5 trials. Change one contact feature; keep battery, lamp, wires and procedure fixed. Teacher checks enclosed low-voltage batteries and a compatible bulb. No mains, loose button cells, damaged cells, direct shorts or hot wires. Stop if parts warm. Adults handle cutting and real safety decisions. Observe five closed-switch trials and record every outcome. Observe five open-switch trials and record every outcome. Explain one contact change from Design 1 evidence; test Design 2 under the same conditions. Record only observations actually available. Compare both designs.
